It's a well-informed assessment — it actually read the repo (it cites `context/post-v1-roadmap.md` twice), and its conclusions land very close to where the project's own self-assessment and the v1.2 plan already are. My take:

**Where I agree, and it's essentially confirming your own roadmap:**
- **~5.5–6/10 with architecture ahead of product maturity** is the same verdict as the July self-assessment, just credited upward for the post-v1 work (assets/lineage/incidents, monitor kinds, pushdown, MCP, LLM seam). Fair adjustment.
- **"Automated discovery is the #1 gap"** — correct, and it's the known gap. Everything today is human-authored; #1512 (LLM check suggestions) is the first step, but it's suggest-on-demand, not fleet-wide "monitor everything by default." The pieces already exist (ADR 0040 inventory sync, the profiler, dimension coverage gaps as NULL) — what's missing is the loop that walks the inventory, profiles, proposes, and gets human approval at scale. Its "one metric to obsess over" (% of assets monitored without manual authoring) is a genuinely good framing worth stealing.
- **"RCA must be deterministic before AI-driven"** — this is exactly the shape #1513 should take, and matches the discipline already applied to NL→SQL (validator-gated, evidence-card UI). Signals → evidence graph → LLM *explains*, never invents. Worth writing into the RCA design explicitly.
- **Pipeline gating as part of the "killer workflow"** — note it lists gating in `Detect → Explain → Impact → Gate → Remediate`, while #1651 is deliberately P3/ADR-gated. That's not a contradiction: its own advice ("deterministic before AI") is the reason the gate is gated. The ADR, when written, should cite this ordering.
- **Production evidence 2.5/10** — accurate and unfixable by code. Solo-dev demo deployments on two clouds are engineering proof, not customer proof.
- **"Data Quality Control Plane" positioning** over "cheaper Monte Carlo" — good framing, consistent with the connection-anchored engines direction (ADR 0036) and the orchestration-first design. The marketing site could adopt this language almost verbatim.

**Where I'd discount it:**
- **The competitor scorecard is vibes, not measurement** — it says so itself, and the numbers come from vendor marketing pages (Monte Carlo "MCP/agent interface: 8", Soda "9" — those are claims from their own product pages, not anything it evaluated). DataQ's MCP surface — 47 curated tools with mutation-verified gates and honesty fields — is plausibly *ahead* of what those vendors actually ship, not a point behind. Directionally use the table, don't trust individual cells.
- **"Anomaly 4/10" undersells slightly but not much** — rolling z-score with seasonality per-check is real; what's missing is it being fleet-wide and automatic rather than a monitor kind you opt into, which is the same automated-discovery gap restated.
- It gives no credit for things it likely couldn't see from docs alone: the compliance track (G1–G5), the redaction ladder, the test-discipline culture. "Governance 6/10" is probably a point or two low for a product this age.

**Net:** the assessment is worth keeping — the five priority gaps it names (discovery, unknown-unknowns, deterministic RCA, scale benchmarks, ecosystem integrations) are a defensible v1.3+ theme list, and gaps 1–3 map cleanly onto the W4 feature set already filed (#1512/#1513) plus the anomaly-kind promotion. The one thing it names that nothing on the roadmap covers is **scale benchmarks** ("what happens at 50k assets / 1M checks") — v1.2 W6 is perf week, which would be the natural place to produce the first real numbers.

gh issue create -R TheurgicDuke771/DataQ \
  --title "feat: automated coverage loop — fleet-wide monitor bootstrap over the asset inventory (G-a remainder)" \
  --label enhancement --label "priority/P2" --milestone "v1.2 Backlog" \
  --body "## Context

An external competitive review of DataQ (ChatGPT deep-dive against the public repo, 2026-08-29) named **automated discovery as the #1 product gap**, matching our own roadmap's G-a (\"monitors only what you remember to check\"). The category leaders' pitch is the inverse of ours:

> DataQ: \"Tell me what quality means and I'll execute it reliably.\"
> Monte Carlo / Soda / Anomalo: \"I'll figure out what should be monitored.\"

What has shipped so far attacks G-a per-suite and on-demand: the monitor kinds (freshness/volume/schema_drift/anomaly, #426/#437/#592/#593), the profiler, ADR 0040 inventory sync (unmonitored assets are at least *visible*), dimension coverage gaps (ADR 0038 — NULL renders as a gap), and the W4 LLM check suggestions (#1513, profiler-driven, catalog-constrained). None of it closes the fleet-wide loop.

## Ask

A coverage loop that walks the ADR-0040 asset inventory and bootstraps monitoring without a human authoring each check:

\`\`\`
inventory (ADR 0040 sync)
  → profile
  → infer dimensions + patterns
  → suggest checks/monitors (reuses #1513's suggestion engine)
  → human approval queue (batch approve/reject — approval stays mandatory)
  → continuous monitoring
\`\`\`

Plus **the metric the whole feature exists for**, surfaced on the dashboard:

> **% of production data assets continuously monitored without manually authored checks**

That number (and its false-positive companion rate) is the honest measure of whether DataQ is becoming an observability platform rather than a check runner.

## Scope notes
- Human approval is a hard requirement — machine-*discovered*, human-*approved* (never silent auto-apply; consistent with the #1651 gating caution and the LLM validator-gate discipline).
- Reuses existing seams: profiler, monitor kinds, #1513 suggestion path, ADR 0040 inventory. No new schema expected beyond an approval-queue state.
- Cost control matters: profiling a whole inventory is warehouse compute — needs batching/sampling and an opt-in per connection, like inventory sync itself.
- Companion: the zero-config baseline half (unknown-unknowns) is deliberately a separate issue — this one is about *authoring automation*, that one about *baselines without checks*.

Refs: context/post-v1-roadmap.md G-a / Theme 2, #1513, ADR 0038, ADR 0040." --json number,url 2>/dev/null || gh issue create -R TheurgicDuke771/DataQ \
  --title "feat: automated coverage loop — fleet-wide monitor bootstrap over the asset inventory (G-a remainder)" \
  --label enhancement --label "priority/P2" --milestone "v1.2 Backlog" \
  --body-file /dev/null

gh issue create -R TheurgicDuke771/DataQ \
  --title "feat(monitors): zero-config auto-baselines — unknown-unknown detection without an authored check" \
  --label enhancement --label "priority/P2" --milestone "v1.2 Backlog" \
  --body "## Context

Companion to #1660 (same external-review finding, 2026-08-29; roadmap gap G-a). The \`anomaly\` monitor kind (#593) is real but **opt-in per check**: someone must author an anomaly check on a specific metric of a specific target before a baseline exists. Enterprise observability's core promise is the inverse:

> \"Something changed and nobody told us what to expect.\"

Today an unauthored regression — distribution shift, cardinality collapse, null-rate jump, volume deviation, categorical-value drift, gradually deteriorating freshness — sails past DataQ unless a human predicted it.

## Ask

Promote baselining from a monitor *kind* you author to a first-class per-asset system:

- For assets opted into coverage (per-connection, like ADR 0040 inventory sync), automatically maintain rolling baselines for the cheap universal metrics — row count/volume, freshness, null rates, cardinality, schema shape — without an authored check per metric.
- Deviations surface through the existing seams: \`metric_value\` history, \`monitor_baselines\`, incidents, severity routing. No parallel result pipeline.
- Sensitivity/seasonality config at asset or workspace level, not per-check.
- False-positive rate is a tracked output (see #1660's metric) — an auto-baseline system that cries wolf gets disabled by users and the feature is dead.

## Scope notes
- The z-score + seasonality engine from #593 and the aggregate-stats kind (#1602) are the building blocks; this is orchestration + defaults, not new math.
- Pipeline-runtime anomalies are already separately filed (#1653).
- Cold-start behaviour must stay honest (skip, not fabricate — #593 precedent).

Refs: #1660, #593, #1602, #1653, ADR 0012, ADR 0040."

- Prerequisite #389 (channel-neutral rename) is closed, so this is unblocked.
- Fits naturally beside #1514 (reusable notification channels) — a webhook channel is just another channel type there.

Externally prompted: a 2026-08-29 competitive review named the enterprise ecosystem (PagerDuty/Jira/ServiceNow/Datadog/…) as one of five priority gaps; this publisher + the template layer (filed separately) is the zero-vendor-code way our ResultPublisher seam covers it. Bidirectional/ITSM-grade sync stays Theme 14, deliberately out of scope.

Refs: #1514, #389 (closed), ADR 0010." && gh issue create -R TheurgicDuke771/DataQ \
  --title "feat(alerting): per-destination payload templates + auth header on the webhook publisher (PagerDuty / Opsgenie / ServiceNow / Jira)" \
  --label enhancement --label "priority/P3" --milestone "v1.2 Backlog" \
  --body "Files the second \"_(no issue yet)_\" roadmap row (context/post-v1-roadmap.md Theme 5), stacked on the generic outbound-webhook publisher (see the issue filed just before this one).

A thin template layer over the generic webhook gives **create-only** coverage of:
- PagerDuty (Events API v2)
- Opsgenie
- ServiceNow (inbound REST)
- Jira (Automation inbound webhooks)

with **zero vendor-specific code** in DataQ — each destination is a payload template + an auth header, both user-supplied config. Bidirectional/ITSM-grade sync (ack/resolve flowing back) is Theme 14 and deliberately separate.

Same redaction guarantee as all alert surfaces; template output must pass the redaction ladder, and a template must not be able to reach fields the alert payload doesn't already expose (no new exfiltration primitive — the #1118/#1401 class).

Refs: the generic webhook publisher issue, #1514, context/post-v1-roadmap.md Theme 5 + Theme 14."
